alignments.note: `יָכֹל` with its subject pronoun; the ASV writes the negation and the modal as two words (*mayest not*), which rule 35 says defeats the indivisible *cannot* reading, so the modal belongs to this verb.
The modal takes a bare complement (*mayest not sacrifice*), so no *to* is written for this `לְ` (rule 52's closing sentence).
H853 object marker; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).

Construct numeral `אַחַד` rendered *any* in the negated clause. It keeps only its own word: rule 19's third sentence gives the relational expression of a construct chain to the nomen rectum, and that rule expressly forbids reading such an *of* as part of an English quantifier (`כֹּל` takes *all*, never *all of*). Giving `אֶחָד` the whole *any of* was the accepted reading and is what this correction reverses.

Nomen rectum of `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` takes the relational *of* together with its own word, headed on the noun (rule 19); the unit is discontinuous around the possessive under rule 25, exactly as `יָדֶיךָ` → *of ... hands* is elsewhere.
Dative `לְ` rendered as a bare English indirect object (rule 40).

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment kept *any of* whole on the construct numeral `אַחַד`. `אַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ` is an ordinary construct chain, so rule 19 puts the relational *of* on the nomen rectum and leaves the construct only its own word; the rule's `כֻּלָּם` → *all of them* paragraph is directly on point and forbids reading the *of* as part of an English quantifier.
`לֹא תוּכַל` is split rather than fused: the ASV writes *mayest not*, two words, which rule 35 says defeats the indivisible `cannot` reading.
Both `לְ`s of the verse (before the infinitive and the dative before the suffix) are `unrepresented`, each because the ASV's recasting writes no word for the relation.
